differences.title: PDF 2.0 UTF-8 annotation contents are decoded as legacy text
differences.expectation: A PDF 2.0 annotation Contents string beginning with the UTF-8 BOM is decoded as UTF-8 and returns the encoded Thai text.
differences.playa_behavior: The UTF-8 BOM and annotation bytes are decoded as legacy single-byte text, producing mojibake and an embedded NUL.
differences.reproduction: Open `PDF 2.0 UTF-8 string and annotation.pdf` and read the first annotation's Contents value.

differences.title: Unknown filter in optional linearization data prevents normal document processing
differences.expectation: An unknown filter in an optional linearization cross-reference stream is ignored so the main cross-reference data, pages, and ordinary page contents remain available.
differences.playa_behavior: Opening the test file aborts while decoding the optional linearization data, before ordinary document processing can continue.
differences.reproduction: Open `UnknownFilter-Linearized.pdf`, enumerate its pages, and extract the visible page text. Document processing aborts before those operations complete.

differences.title: Unknown filter in optional outline object stream prevents page access
differences.expectation: A hybrid-reference PDF remains available for page enumeration, text extraction, and image extraction when an unknown filter affects only the object stream containing optional outline objects; the outline itself may be unavailable.
differences.playa_behavior: After hybrid cross-reference parsing fails, fallback object scanning eagerly expands every object stream and aborts on the unknown filter before the otherwise independent page tree can be accessed.
differences.reproduction: Open `UnknownFilter-OutlineObjStm.pdf`, enumerate its pages, and extract the visible page text or image. Accessing the page list aborts before those operations can run.

differences.title: DCTDecode image extraction writes PNG polyglot bytes with a JPEG extension
differences.expectation: Strict DCT stream handling rejects bytes that do not begin with the JPEG SOI marker, rather than format-sniffing or scanning embedded data into an alternate visible image.
differences.playa_behavior: Image extraction chooses a `.jpg` suffix from the declared DCTDecode filter and writes the stream unchanged even though its first eight bytes are the PNG signature.
differences.reproduction: Open the hash-named PDF, find the page image whose XObject name is `Ig2`, and compare the suffix selected by `get_image_suffix_and_writer()` with the first eight bytes of its stream.

differences.title: DCTDecode image extraction writes PNG polyglot bytes with a JPEG extension
differences.expectation: Strict DCT stream handling rejects bytes that do not begin with the JPEG SOI marker, rather than format-sniffing or scanning embedded data into an alternate visible image.
differences.playa_behavior: Image extraction chooses a `.jpg` suffix from the declared DCTDecode filter and writes the stream unchanged even though its first eight bytes are the PNG signature.
differences.reproduction: Open the hash-named PDF, find the page image whose XObject name is `Ig2`, and compare the suffix selected by `get_image_suffix_and_writer()` with the first eight bytes of its stream.

differences.title: Indexed color-space indices are not rounded or clamped
differences.expectation: An Indexed color component is rounded to the nearest integer with 0.5 ties rounded upward, then clamped to the inclusive range from zero through hival.
differences.playa_behavior: Interpreted path graphics states retain the authored -17, 6.5, and 17 components instead of exposing the effective 0, 7, and 7 indices for an Indexed color space whose hival is 7.
differences.reproduction: Open `IndexedCS_negative_and_high.pdf`, enumerate page paths whose nonstroking color space is `Cs1`, and inspect each path's nonstroking color values.

differences.title: Page and screen path coordinates ignore the page UserUnit
differences.expectation: The page's UserUnit value participates in the initial transformation from default user space to page or screen device space, so interpreted path segments reflect the declared scale.
differences.playa_behavior: Interpreted path segments in page and screen space retain the unscaled default-user-space X coordinates even though the page declares UserUnit 10.
differences.reproduction: Open `LineCap-Degenerate.pdf` with `space="page"` or `space="screen"`, then compare the first point of each path's `raw_segments` and interpreted `segments`.

differences.title: Structure element ActualText is ignored during text extraction
differences.expectation: ActualText on the Span structure element replaces the erroneous invisible OCR text, yielding the extractable sentence shown by the PDF Association test.
differences.playa_behavior: The ActualText property is exposed on the structure element, but both the element text and tagged page extraction return the erroneous invisible OCR text instead.

differences.title: Document font discovery misses fonts nested in Type 3 resources
differences.expectation: Document-wide font discovery descends through Type 3 font resource dictionaries and reports FType3A, FType3B, and Helvetica.
differences.playa_behavior: Only the top-level page font FType3A is reported; the nested Type 3 font FType3B and its Helvetica resource are omitted.
differences.reproduction: Open `FontinsideType3insideType3.pdf` and enumerate `document.fonts`.

differences.title: Type 3 explicit encoding is replaced by StandardEncoding when its glyph names have no Unicode mapping
differences.expectation: A Type 3 font's required Encoding entirely defines its character-code mapping. Codes absent from that explicit encoding, and glyph names without a Unicode mapping, remain unmapped.
differences.playa_behavior: Because the explicit glyph names `rect` and `triangle` produce no Unicode mappings, the complete encoding is replaced with StandardEncoding. Unspecified codes such as 32 and 65 then decode as a space and `A`, while the explicitly named glyphs decode as `a` and `b`.
differences.reproduction: Open `FontinsideType3insideType3.pdf`, get the FType3A font, inspect its explicit Encoding Differences, and decode character codes 32, 65, 97, and 98.

differences.title: Document font discovery misses fonts nested in Pattern resources
differences.expectation: Document-wide font discovery descends into Pattern resource dictionaries and reports both Helvetica and Times-Italic.
differences.playa_behavior: Only the top-level Helvetica page font is reported; Times-Italic inside the Pattern resource is omitted.
differences.reproduction: Open `PatternTextInsideText.pdf` and enumerate `document.fonts`.

differences.title: Indirect object references are accepted in content streams
differences.expectation: Indirect object references are not part of the content-stream object grammar, so encountering one directly or inside a content-stream dictionary produces a syntax error.
differences.playa_behavior: The content parser accepts indirect object references in operands and nested dictionaries and emits content objects instead of reporting invalid content-stream syntax.
differences.reproduction: Open `Dialect-ContentStreamsWithIndirectRefs.pdf` and enumerate `document.pages[0].contents`; the invalid references are accepted without a syntax error.

differences.title: Dictionary referenced as a content stream is silently treated as empty content
differences.expectation: A dictionary without the required stream and endstream keywords remains a dictionary. Using it as page Contents is invalid PDF syntax and produces an observable type or syntax error.
differences.playa_behavior: The non-stream Contents value produces a warning, but content enumeration continues with an empty buffer and returns no content objects or error.
differences.reproduction: Open `Dialect-StreamIsDict.pdf` and enumerate `document.pages[0].contents`; the plain dictionary is silently represented as empty page content.

differences.go_error: compare snapshot: decode Playa page 0: resolve Go page 0: playa: page node is not dictionary
differences.title: Stream referenced as a page dictionary is replaced with an empty page
differences.expectation: A stream object remains distinct from its stream dictionary. Using one as a page or font dictionary is invalid PDF syntax and produces an observable type or syntax error.
differences.playa_behavior: The invalid page stream produces a warning, then page traversal substitutes a 612 by 792 empty page and continues without returning an error; the fixture's `Dict is Stream` text is lost.
differences.reproduction: Open `Dialect-DictIsStream.pdf`, enumerate `document.pages`, and extract text from the first page; an empty synthesized page is returned instead of a syntax error.

differences.title: UTF-16LE text strings are decoded as Unicode despite being excluded by the PDF text-string grammar
differences.expectation: ISO 32000-2 permits PDFDocEncoding, UTF-16BE, and UTF-8 text strings, but not UTF-16LE. A string beginning with `FF FE` therefore remains a PDFDocEncoding byte sequence rather than being decoded as UTF-16LE.
differences.playa_behavior: A leading `FF FE` byte pair is treated as a UTF-16 byte-order marker. Page-label prefixes and outline titles are consequently decoded into Unicode symbols instead of retaining their distinguishable PDFDocEncoding byte values.
differences.reproduction: Open `utf16LE-test.pdf`, read the first page label and enumerate the outline titles.

differences.title: Text clipping at ET does not update the clipping path
differences.expectation: Glyph outlines shown in a clipping rendering mode accumulate until ET, when their nonzero-winding union intersects the current clipping path before later paths are painted.
differences.playa_behavior: The blue rectangle painted after ET retains a graphics state with no clipping path, so the text clipping operation is not observable.
differences.reproduction: Open `OverlappingGlyphClipping.pdf`, enumerate the first page's paths, and inspect the graphics state of the blue rectangle painted after ET.

differences.title: Text clipping mode changes are discarded at ET
differences.expectation: All glyphs shown while the rendering mode includes clipping accumulate within the text object, regardless of changes among modes 4 through 7, and update the clipping path exactly once at ET.
differences.playa_behavior: Each path painted after a clipping text object retains a graphics state with no clipping path, including text objects that change between clipping rendering modes.
differences.reproduction: Open `TextClippingModeChanges.pdf`, enumerate the first page's three paths, and inspect each path's graphics state after the preceding ET operator.

upstream_issues.title: PDF 2.0 UTF-8 text strings with a BOM are decoded as PDFDocEncoding
upstream_issues.summary:
PDF 2.0 text strings beginning with the UTF-8 BOM (`EF BB BF`) are decoded as PDFDocEncoding. This leaves the BOM as mojibake and corrupts non-ASCII text.

The issue affects several kinds of PDF text strings, including page-label prefixes, outline titles, and annotation contents.
upstream_issues.reproduction:
```python
import playa

with playa.open("pdf20-utf8-test.pdf") as document:
    print(repr(document.pages[0].label))
    print([repr(item.title) for item in document.outline])

with playa.open("PDF 2.0 UTF-8 string and annotation.pdf") as document:
    annotation = next(iter(document.pages[0].annotations))
    print(repr(annotation.contents))
```
upstream_issues.actual_behavior:
The first file produces values including:

```text
'ï»¿Prefixi'
'ï»¿PDF 2.0 with UTF-8 test file'
```

The annotation contents are also mojibake and contain an embedded NUL:

```text
'ï»¿à¹—à¸®à¹—à¸¥à¸Łà¹„à¸‡à¹›à¸\x00à¸—à¸§à¸²à¸¡'
```
upstream_issues.expected_behavior:
The UTF-8 BOM should be removed and the remaining bytes decoded as UTF-8. Representative values should be:

```text
'Prefixi'
'PDF 2.0 with UTF-8 test file'
'ไฮไลต์ข้อความ'
```
upstream_issues.relevant_implementation: `playa.utils.decode_text()` currently recognizes UTF-16 BOMs before falling back to PDFDocEncoding, but does not recognize the PDF 2.0 UTF-8 BOM.

upstream_issues.title: Unknown filter in optional linearization data prevents normal document processing
upstream_issues.summary: A PDF whose optional Linearization data uses an unknown stream filter cannot be processed normally. Accessing the page list aborts with `NotImplementedError`, even though the main cross-reference information and ordinary page contents remain usable when the optional Linearization data is ignored.
upstream_issues.reproduction:
```python
import playa

with playa.open("UnknownFilter-Linearized.pdf") as document:
    print(len(document.pages))
    print(document.pages[0].extract_text())
```
upstream_issues.actual_behavior:
Accessing `document.pages` aborts while loading the cross-reference data:

```text
NotImplementedError: Unsupported filter: /'XXXDecode'
```

The exception originates while decoding a stream from the cross-reference loading path, before normal page processing can proceed.
upstream_issues.expected_behavior: Because the stream belongs to optional Linearization data, it should be possible to ignore that data and use the main cross-reference information. The document should remain available for page enumeration and ordinary content extraction.
upstream_issues.relevant_implementation: The failure occurs along `Document._read_xrefs_into()` → `XRefStream._load()` → `ContentStream.decode()` while the optional Linearization cross-reference stream is decoded.

upstream_issues.title: Unknown filter in optional outline object stream prevents page access
upstream_issues.summary: A hybrid-reference PDF cannot expose its page list when an unknown stream filter affects only an incremental-update object stream containing optional outline objects. Hybrid cross-reference parsing falls back to object scanning, which eagerly expands that unrelated object stream and aborts before the original page tree can be used.
upstream_issues.reproduction:
```python
import playa

with playa.open("UnknownFilter-OutlineObjStm.pdf") as document:
    print(len(document.pages))
    print(document.pages[0].extract_text())
    print(len(list(document.pages[0].images)))
```
upstream_issues.actual_behavior:
Accessing `document.pages` first reports a hybrid cross-reference parsing failure, enters fallback object scanning, and then aborts while eagerly expanding the outline object stream:

```text
NotImplementedError: Unsupported filter: /'XXXDecode'
```

Page enumeration, text extraction, and image extraction never run.
upstream_issues.expected_behavior: The unknown filter affects only the object stream containing three optional outline objects. The existing page tree and its ordinary contents should remain available for page enumeration, text extraction, and image extraction; the outline itself may be unavailable with a warning or scoped error.
upstream_issues.relevant_implementation: `Document._read_xrefs()` enters `XRefFallback` after hybrid cross-reference parsing raises `PDFSyntaxError`. `XRefFallback._load()` then expands every discovered `/ObjStm` immediately via `stream.buffer`, so an unsupported filter in an optional object stream aborts reconstruction globally.

upstream_issues.title: DCTDecode image extraction writes PNG polyglot bytes with a JPEG extension
upstream_issues.summary: Image extraction trusts the declared `/DCTDecode` filter when choosing a `.jpg` suffix, but does not validate that the stream is JPEG data. In two PDF Association real-world samples, the affected stream begins with a PNG signature and contains polyglot data that different decoders can interpret as different visible images.
upstream_issues.reproduction:
```python
from playa.image import get_image_suffix_and_writer
import playa

files = (
    "382252277877c00a92f3bb54daef1413bafe5557e2f5f7c32c23e800cd9bdcd4.pdf",
    "4387ba480c6f935b8e97749d40b3c001ad584b7bda66ca2c040be67337669497.pdf",
)
for filename in files:
    with playa.open(filename) as document:
        image = next(image for image in document.pages[0].images if image.xobjid == "Ig2")
        suffix, _ = get_image_suffix_and_writer(image.stream)
        print(filename, suffix, image.stream.buffer[:8].hex())
```
upstream_issues.actual_behavior:
For both files the selected suffix is `.jpg`, while the reported leading bytes are the PNG signature:

```text
.jpg 89504e470d0a1a0a
```

The CLI consequently writes PNG polyglot bytes to a file whose extension is `.jpg` without warning or error.
upstream_issues.expected_behavior: A stream declared as `/DCTDecode` should be validated as JPEG data before it is exported as `.jpg`. If the stream does not begin with the JPEG SOI marker, extraction should report a scoped decoding error or omit the invalid image rather than writing or format-sniffing the polyglot payload.
upstream_issues.relevant_implementation: `playa.image.get_image_suffix_and_writer()` returns `.jpg` and a raw writer as soon as it sees a DCTDecode filter. The writer receives `stream.buffer` without checking that the bytes are a JPEG stream.

upstream_issues.title: Indexed color-space indices are not rounded or clamped
upstream_issues.summary: Interpreted graphics-state colors preserve out-of-range and fractional components for Indexed color spaces. This exposes values that do not represent the effective palette index required by the PDF color-space rules.
upstream_issues.reproduction:
```python
import playa

with playa.open("IndexedCS_negative_and_high.pdf") as document:
    indices = [
        path.gstate.ncolor.values[0]
        for path in document.pages[0].paths
        if path.gstate.ncs.name == "Cs1"
    ]
    print(indices)
```
upstream_issues.actual_behavior:
For the Indexed color space with `hival=7`, the interpreted path colors are:

```text
[-17, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 6.5, 17]
```

The negative, fractional tie, and high values remain unchanged.
upstream_issues.expected_behavior:
Indexed color components are rounded to the nearest integer, with 0.5 ties rounded upward, and then clamped to the range from zero through `hival`. The effective indices should therefore be:

```text
[0, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 7, 7]
```
upstream_issues.relevant_implementation: `ColorSpace.make_color()` converts operands with `num_value()` but does not inspect an Indexed color space's `spec` or `hival`; `PDFPageInterpreter.do_SCN()` and `do_scn()` therefore store the raw component unchanged.

upstream_issues.title: Page and screen path coordinates ignore the page UserUnit
upstream_issues.summary: When a page declares `/UserUnit 10`, interpreted path segments returned in `page` and `screen` device spaces retain their unscaled default-user-space coordinates. The resulting device-space path geometry is ten times smaller than the scale declared by the page.
upstream_issues.reproduction:
```python
import playa

for space in ("page", "screen"):
    with playa.open("LineCap-Degenerate.pdf", space=space) as document:
        path = next(iter(document.pages[0].paths))
        raw = path.raw_segments[0].points[0]
        device = next(path.segments).points[0]
        print(space, raw, device)
```
upstream_issues.actual_behavior: The first path starts at X=10 in default user space. In both tested device spaces, its interpreted X coordinate is also 10. The remaining paths likewise keep their raw X coordinates.
upstream_issues.expected_behavior: The page declares `/UserUnit 10`, so the initial transform for `page` and `screen` space should include that scale. The first interpreted path X coordinate should therefore be 100, while the raw segment remains at X=10. The `default` space can remain the identity transform.
upstream_issues.relevant_implementation: `Page.set_initial_ctm()` builds the page and screen transforms from the MediaBox and rotation, but does not include the page's inherited `UserUnit` value.

upstream_issues.title: Structure element ActualText is ignored during text extraction
upstream_issues.summary: When `/ActualText` is attached to a structure element rather than the marked-content property list, the replacement is available through `Element.actual_text` but is not used by `Element.text` or `Page.extract_text_tagged()`. As a result, erroneous invisible OCR text is returned instead of the intended replacement.
upstream_issues.reproduction:
```python
import playa

with playa.open("UA1_Tpdf-G2_06.pdf") as document:
    page = document.pages[0]
    span = page.structure.find("Span")
    print(repr(span.actual_text))
    print(repr(span.text))
    print(repr(page.extract_text_tagged()))
```
upstream_issues.actual_behavior:
The structure property is decoded correctly, but the two extraction paths return the OCR errors:

```text
'Available 24/7, you can book an appointment online.'
'Availal;!e 24/7, you c;m book an appointroP.nt online.'
'Availal;!e 24/7, you c;m book an appointroP.nt online.'
```
upstream_issues.expected_behavior:
Both `span.text` and `page.extract_text_tagged()` should use the structure element's replacement text:

```text
'Available 24/7, you can book an appointment online.'
```
upstream_issues.relevant_implementation: `Element.actual_text` reads the structure element property, but `Element.text` joins `ContentItem.text`, while both `ContentItem.text` and `Page.extract_text_tagged()` only inspect `ActualText` on the marked-content property list.

upstream_issues.title: Document.fonts misses fonts nested in Type 3 and Pattern resources
upstream_issues.summary: `Document.fonts` only discovers fonts directly listed in each page's Font resources. Fonts reachable through nested resource dictionaries are omitted, including fonts inside Type 3 fonts and Pattern resources.
upstream_issues.reproduction:
```python
import playa

for path in (
    "FontinsideType3insideType3.pdf",
    "PatternTextInsideText.pdf",
):
    with playa.open(path) as document:
        print(path, list(document.fonts))
```
upstream_issues.actual_behavior: The nested Type 3 fixture reports only `['FType3A']`; it omits FType3B and Helvetica. The Pattern fixture reports only `['Helvetica']`; it omits Times-Italic.
upstream_issues.expected_behavior: Document-wide font discovery should recursively traverse reachable resource dictionaries. The nested Type 3 fixture should report FType3A, FType3B, and Helvetica, while the Pattern fixture should report Helvetica and Times-Italic.
upstream_issues.relevant_implementation: `document.FontMapping._iteritems()` builds its mapping exclusively from `page.fonts.values()`. It does not traverse resource dictionaries reachable through Type 3 fonts, Patterns, or other nested resources.

upstream_issues.title: Type 3 explicit Encoding is replaced by StandardEncoding when glyph names are unrecognized
upstream_issues.summary: A Type 3 font with an explicit Encoding Differences array using non-AGL glyph names has its entire mapping replaced by StandardEncoding. This invents Unicode text for codes that the font did not map and changes the meaning of explicitly mapped codes.
upstream_issues.reproduction:
```python
import playa

with playa.open("FontinsideType3insideType3.pdf") as document:
    font = document.fonts["FType3A"]
    print(font.encoding)
    print(list(font.decode(bytes((32, 65, 97, 98)))))
```
upstream_issues.actual_behavior: The explicit encoding is `{97: 'rect', 98: 'triangle'}`, but decoding returns a space, `A`, `a`, and `b` for codes 32, 65, 97, and 98. The replacement therefore maps both unspecified codes and explicitly named glyphs through StandardEncoding.
upstream_issues.expected_behavior: A Type 3 font's mapping is entirely defined by its required Encoding entry. Codes 32 and 65 are unspecified and should remain unmapped; the non-AGL glyph names at 97 and 98 also have no justified Unicode text mapping.
upstream_issues.relevant_implementation: `SimpleFont.__init__()` replaces an empty `_cid2unicode` map with `LITERAL_STANDARD_CID2UNICODE`. For Type 3 fonts, this fallback overrides an explicit Encoding whose glyph names are valid for painting but absent from the Adobe Glyph List. This is related to, but narrower than, the heuristic introduced for issue #120.

upstream_issues.title: Indirect object references are accepted in content streams
upstream_issues.summary: The content-stream parser accepts indirect object references even though the content-stream object grammar excludes them. The references may appear as direct operands or inside dictionaries and arrays without producing a syntax error.
upstream_issues.reproduction:
```python
import playa

with playa.open("Dialect-ContentStreamsWithIndirectRefs.pdf") as document:
    print(list(document.pages[0].contents))
```
upstream_issues.actual_behavior: Page content enumeration completes and yields content objects containing or following the indirect references. No invalid-content-stream syntax error is reported.
upstream_issues.expected_behavior: Encountering an indirect reference directly or recursively inside a content-stream object should report invalid content-stream syntax.
upstream_issues.relevant_implementation: The generic object parser recognizes `integer integer R` as an object reference in content streams without a content-specific grammar check that rejects references, including references nested in arrays and dictionaries.

upstream_issues.title: Stream and dictionary object-kind mismatches are recovered as empty content
upstream_issues.summary: Stream objects and plain dictionaries are syntactically distinct in PDF, but object-kind mismatches in page structures are downgraded to warnings and hidden by recovery. A dictionary used as page Contents becomes empty content, while a stream used as a page dictionary becomes a synthesized empty page.
upstream_issues.reproduction:
```python
import playa

for path in (
    "Dialect-StreamIsDict.pdf",
    "Dialect-DictIsStream.pdf",
):
    with playa.open(path) as document:
        page = document.pages[0]
        print(path, page.mediabox, list(page.contents), repr(page.extract_text()))
```
upstream_issues.actual_behavior:
For `Dialect-StreamIsDict.pdf`, Playa logs `Found non-stream in contents` and returns an empty contents sequence without raising an error.

For `Dialect-DictIsStream.pdf`, Playa logs `Missing or invalid page object 4`, substitutes an empty 612 by 792 page, and returns empty contents and text without raising an error.
upstream_issues.expected_behavior: The missing `stream`/`endstream` delimiters in the first file and the unexpected stream wrappers in the second file are PDF syntax errors. The object-kind mismatch should remain observable to callers as a type or syntax error. If recovery is retained, it should not silently replace the malformed objects without an error channel.
upstream_issues.relevant_implementation: `ContentParser.__init__()` catches `TypeError` from `stream_value()` and initializes an empty parser buffer; `Page.streams` catches the same error and skips the object. In the inverse case, `Pages._get_pages()` catches `TypeError` from `dict_value()` and creates a synthetic empty page.

upstream_issues.title: UTF-16LE text strings are decoded as Unicode despite being excluded by PDF
upstream_issues.summary: Text strings beginning with `FF FE` are decoded as UTF-16LE. ISO 32000-2 only defines PDFDocEncoding, UTF-16BE, and UTF-8 for text strings, so accepting the little-endian form changes the observable values of malformed strings and creates a parser differential.
upstream_issues.reproduction:
```python
import playa

with playa.open("utf16LE-test.pdf") as document:
    print(repr(document.pages[0].label))
    print([repr(item.title) for item in document.outline])
```
upstream_issues.actual_behavior: The `FF FE` prefix is treated as a UTF-16 byte-order marker. The page-label prefix decodes as `∰`, and the three outline titles decode as `∰㉐⑊`, `∰✴㉐`, and `㉐入⑊`.
upstream_issues.expected_behavior: Because UTF-16LE is not a permitted PDF text-string encoding, `FF FE` should not select Unicode decoding. The bytes should remain distinguishable under the PDFDocEncoding fallback used for text strings without a recognized permitted encoding marker.
upstream_issues.relevant_implementation: `playa.utils.decode_text()` explicitly accepts both `FE FF` and `FF FE`, then passes the bytes to Python's BOM-sensitive `UTF-16` decoder. The `FF FE` branch is the behavior exercised by this test.

upstream_issues.title: Expose the clipping path, somehow
upstream_issues.summary: Path clipping and text clipping are not represented in the interpreted graphics state, so content painted after a clipping operation cannot expose that the clipping path changed.
upstream_issues.reproduction:
```python
import playa

for filename in (
    "OverlappingGlyphClipping.pdf",
    "TextClippingModeChanges.pdf",
):
    with playa.open(filename) as document:
        print(filename, [path.gstate.clipping_path for path in document.pages[0].paths])
```
upstream_issues.actual_behavior: Every printed value is `None`. Glyphs shown in clipping rendering modes are discarded at ET instead of updating the clipping path carried by subsequent path graphics states.
upstream_issues.expected_behavior: The accumulated glyph outlines should intersect the current clipping path at ET. Subsequent content should expose a non-empty clipping path until Q restores the prior graphics state.
upstream_issues.relevant_implementation: `GraphicState.clipping_path` is still declared as `None` with a TODO, while `PDFPageInterpreter.do_W()`, `do_W_a()`, and `do_ET()` have empty bodies on current main.

upstream_issues.title: Tagged text extraction follows content-stream order instead of structure-tree order
upstream_issues.summary: `Page.extract_text_tagged()` emits marked text in content-stream painting order. When a tagged PDF's structure tree deliberately defines a different logical order, extraction ignores that order; correctly tagged sidebar placement is changed, while intentionally invalid order samples can appear visually repaired.
upstream_issues.reproduction:
```python
import playa

for filename in (
    "UA1_Tpdf-G4_04.pdf",
    "UA1_Tpdf-G4_F01.pdf",
    "UA1_Tpdf-G4_F02.pdf",
):
    with playa.open(filename) as document:
        print(filename)
        print(document.pages[0].extract_text_tagged())
```
upstream_issues.actual_behavior: For `UA1_Tpdf-G4_04.pdf`, the sidebar is emitted before the H1 because it is painted first, although the structure tree places it after the H1. For `UA1_Tpdf-G4_F01.pdf`, extraction emits the visually ordered H1 and paragraphs rather than the deliberately invalid structure order beginning with `FAIL` and the second paragraph. For `UA1_Tpdf-G4_F02.pdf`, the two paragraphs are emitted in painting order rather than the explicit marked-content order inside their structure elements.
upstream_issues.expected_behavior: Tagged text extraction should follow the structure tree's `/K` order both between elements and between marked-content references within an element. The correctly tagged sidebar sample should emit the H1 before the sidebar, and the intentionally invalid samples should preserve their invalid logical order so that each failure remains observable.
upstream_issues.relevant_implementation: `Page.extract_text_tagged()` iterates `self.flatten(...)` and groups consecutive text objects by marked-content section. It does not traverse `document.structure` or use structure-element content order when deciding the output sequence.

upstream_issues.title: Element.attributes drops structure attribute arrays without explicit revision numbers
upstream_issues.summary: `Element.attributes` treats every structure attribute array as strict attribute-object/revision-number pairs. PDF revision numbers are optional, so valid arrays containing unversioned attribute dictionaries return `None` and hide attributes such as `BBox`, `ListNumbering`, and `Placement`.
upstream_issues.reproduction:
```python
import playa

for filename in (
    "UA1_Tpdf-L_06.pdf",
    "UA1_Tpdf-L_10.pdf",
):
    with playa.open(filename) as document:
        print(filename)
        for element in document.structure.find_all("L"):
            print(element.props.get("A"), element.attributes)
```
upstream_issues.actual_behavior: For `UA1_Tpdf-L_06.pdf`, the raw `A` value contains one List attribute dictionary with `ListNumbering=None`, but `element.attributes` returns `None`. For the ordered inline list in `UA1_Tpdf-L_10.pdf`, the raw array contains both a List dictionary with `ListNumbering=LowerRoman` and a Layout dictionary with `Placement=Inline`, but `element.attributes` again returns `None`. The same pattern hides unversioned `BBox` attributes on the referenced Figure samples.
upstream_issues.expected_behavior: Every attribute object in the array should remain accessible. An attribute object not followed by an integer has revision 0; consecutive unversioned dictionaries must not be interpreted as an invalid object/revision pair. The API may expose the objects individually or as a documented combined view, but it should preserve attributes from all of them.
upstream_issues.relevant_implementation: `Element.attributes` iterates `for attrdict, revision in choplist(2, attrs)` and rejects each pair unless the second value is an integer. This assumes revision numbers are mandatory and also prevents multiple unversioned attribute objects from being represented.
